### Implementation decisions

A current cycle IDR is a retained JSON object with `cycle_id`, `kind: "idr"`,
`name`, positive `revision`, `contents`, and `at`. `contents` requires nonempty
`alternatives`, `approach`, `assumptions`, `constraints`, and `intended_evidence`.
A simplify selection adds `assessed`, `proposals`, and `selected` under its
local contract. Each proposal contains exactly `id`, `removes`,
`retained_behavior`, `objectives`, `decision_clauses`, `expected_savings`,
`verification`, and `paths`. `id`, `removes`, `retained_behavior`,
`expected_savings`, and `verification` are nonempty strings. `objectives`,
`decision_clauses`, and `paths` are nonempty lists of nonempty strings.
An absent decision clause is expressed as the sole `none: <reason>` entry.
`assessed` is nonempty text. `selected` is a nonempty list of distinct proposal
IDs drawn from the proposals. Earlier revisions remain preserved.

The cycle's decision reference contains `path`, `sha256`, `kind`, `name`,
`approval`, and `accepted`. A changed subject needs approval of that revision.
Do not reuse a prior approval for modified content. Historical book/run IDRs
have a different schema; do not apply it to cycle IDRs.

Current retained IDRs live under `cycles/<ID>/decisions/`; the writer uses
an immutable randomly named `.json` file. It hashes the exact retained bytes
with SHA-256. `revision` is one above the count of earlier references with the
same name. Creating reasoning is permitted only in Plan or Build, before
dependent implementation; quick-fix must change type for a material decision.
Do not add an approval reference before genuine approval of those bytes.
Replacing an approach preserves earlier revisions and creates no architectural
authority. A pending IDR can be useful without claiming its approach was approved.

### Reviews

The authored cycle review has exactly `reviewer`, `scope`, `evidence`,
`blocking`, `advisory`, `cosmetic`, `verdict`, and `rationale`. The five fields
`scope`, `evidence`, `blocking`, `advisory`, and `cosmetic` are lists. Verdict
is `approve | changes-required`. Each blocker identifies `path`, `consequence`,
and `evidence`. The current writer requires the scope set to equal the plan's
scope and the reviewer to differ from every implementer.

Retention adds `pass`, `scrutiny`, `input_sha256`, `basis_version`,
`basis_sha256`, and `at`. These bind the actual reviewed work and evidence.
A prose review can be useful before retention, but must not pretend to have
those bindings. A blocking review requires the recorded return path before
another approval. Council review of a decision is not implementation review.

`basis_version` is 4 for current retention. Its basis includes the plan content
through the review-bearing phase, required checks, review policy, current-pass
check declaration digests, coverage for version 2, and simplify reduction when
applicable. It excludes task delivery bookkeeping and the plan revision counter.
`input_sha256` separately binds scoped working-tree inputs. Earlier basis
versions retain their algorithms. Missing algorithms or inputs prevent formal
retention; preserve the actual independent report in the inbox rather than
guessing a checksum. A claimed reviewer name cannot establish independence.

### Tests, council, and queue

The appendix embeds test-evidence, council attempt, council result, and queue
schemas. These explain their shape; they do not manufacture the events they
record. Preserve exact subject identity, attribution, failures, and relevant
input/environment bindings. Do not synthesize a passing receipt from a log
fragment or fill a council seat with your own judgment.

Test evidence schema version 2 additionally requires `environment`, `tools`,
`lock_sha256`, and `source_revision`. Version 1 is historical and cannot supply
current reusable environment evidence. A valid receipt needs a closed execution,
sealed record, matching declaration/input/environment identity, and retained
diagnostic log. Record actual invocations, elapsed time, failures, and rerun
reasons in an ordinary note when the evidence engine is absent. Such a note
supports human assessment; it is not a synthesized executable receipt. Preserve
toolchain identity without exposing credentials or secret environment values.

Council records preserve the frozen purpose, subject bytes, policy, model/host
identity, attempts, votes, dissent, and actual architect disposition. Standard
needs two of three provider approvals plus architect agreement addressing
dissent; Strict needs unanimity. Lite needs its two sealed native passes and
actual host evidence. Every mode blocks demonstrated binding failures and
missing authorization. An unavailable model never selects a fallback policy.
Use the owning attestation writer for council outcomes. If unavailable, retain
the request and evidence in the inbox, leaving approval pending.

The queue is at `D/queue/cycles.yaml`. Owner authorization to start queued work
does not authorize publication, extend cycle limits, or approve decisions.
Preserve started-item relationships and authorization bounds. Use its writer
when required, or stage the requested queue change in the inbox.

Queue schema version 1 is YAML containing the embedded JSON-schema shape.
List order is execution order. IDs are unique `Q-NNNN` values below
`next_number`; never reuse one. There are at most 500 lifetime items, including
started ones. Dependencies are unique, resolvable, acyclic, and precede the
dependent item. A started/starting item cannot follow a pending/held item.
Only one item can be starting; two started items cannot name one cycle.

Pending/held items have null `cycle`, `start_token`, and `started_at`; only
held items have a nonempty `hold_reason`. Starting/started items need a genuine
32-hex token; starting has no cycle/time yet, started has both. References
are unique contained repository paths when added. Authorization `started` is
a unique subset of its frozen `scope`; `next` has count 1, `next-n` a positive
integer, and `queue` null. The actual owner instruction must be preserved.
Starting first records an intent, creates a cycle with that token in its
created-history queue origin, then records the cycle identity. After a crash,
reconcile the token against existing cycles before another start. Do not
create authorization or a successful start from inferred owner intent.

## 8. Generated pages and remaining maintenance

Generated architecture, extracted code documentation, ADR indexes and lineage,
summaries, doctrine, and journal indexes derive from other files. Recognize
generated regions inside otherwise editable files as well as generated files.
Edit the source, then run an available regenerator and its drift check.

Without a regenerator, leave generated content intact and record which source
changed and which output needs regeneration. Report the stale view to readers;
do not claim synchronization. Hand-maintained indexes and bidirectional links
still need their normal updates when a record is formally filed.

Finish with what changed, why, what was verified, and what remains. Link the
record containing the detail. Useful continuity matters more than a long report.

Historical promptbooks/runs, implementation-decision YAML, migration packages,
survey receipts, backfill sign-offs, and signed doctrine reconciliations remain
retrievable under their own versioned contracts. Preserve them. This guide does
not teach new historical authoring or synthesize their specialized proof.
For a needed operation outside the supported procedures, retain its exact
proposed change, source references, prerequisite, and responsible actor in the
inbox. Continue authorized independent work that does not depend on it.

## Appendix A. Generated Markdown contracts

These are reproduced canonical definitions, not a second independently authored
schema. Their source locators document provenance and require no installed
plugin to read. In these extracts, `docs/` and `<docs_dir>` mean D. Template
placeholders are illustrative; substitute project facts when creating a record.
Section numbers refer to the source operational schema. A source citation in
an extract names historical context; it is not additional approval evidence.
Project instructions and supported local versions take precedence.

### Objectives contract

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `5.B`.

A single top-level, **hand-authored** file: the product's mission and its goals, the yardstick a decision review measures the decision set against. `init-docs` seeds it from `objectives.md.tmpl` as a placeholder; nothing regenerates it. Its frontmatter carries `maturity`, so a reader knows whether to expect the mission or the goals to move before citing either.

Frontmatter (locked schema — exactly these six keys):

```yaml
---
type: objectives
format_version: "1"
maturity: placeholder | exploring | forming | settled
owner: "<handle>"
reviewed_at: <YYYY-MM-DD>     # last date a human read the file and affirmed or shifted it
review_every_days: <int>      # default 90
---
```

**Maturity ladder (locked).** The value states what may still drift:

| value | what it says |
|---|---|
| `placeholder` | Template untouched. Nothing may cite an `OBJ-N` from it; every reader applies the populate gate below. |
| `exploring` | The mission may still change. Goals are hypotheses. A review reads them as questions, not as a yardstick. |
| `forming` | The mission is fixed. Goals are still being added, split, or dropped. A review measures against the mission and the `active` goals. |
| `settled` | Mission and goals are stable. A change is a Shifts row plus a human read; a review treats an unserved goal as a finding. |

**Body (locked structure).** Exactly three H2 headings, in this order, and nothing else at H2:

```markdown
# Objectives for <repo>

## Mission

<one paragraph, one to three sentences: who it serves, what it does for them, what done well looks like>

## Goals

### OBJ-1 — <short title>
- **kind:** utility | ease-of-use | ux | delivery
- **statement:** <one checkable sentence about the user's outcome, not the code's behavior>
- **measure:** <how you would know> | unmeasured
- **status:** active | achieved | dropped

## Shifts

| date | shifted | from | to | why |
|------|---------|------|----|-----|
| <YYYY-MM-DD> | mission \| OBJ-N | <before> | <after> | <one line> |
```

Goal ids are monotonic from `OBJ-1` and never reused; a dropped goal keeps its heading with `status: dropped`. Shifts rows are newest first and append-only: history above is never rewritten to match a shift.

**Lint rules (`CHK-OBJ-*`, owned by `audit-docs`; each is mechanical):**

- `CHK-OBJ-1` — the file exists; the frontmatter carries exactly the six keys; `maturity` is in the enum; `reviewed_at` is an ISO date not in the future; `review_every_days` is a positive integer.
- `CHK-OBJ-2` — the three H2 headings are present, in order, with no other H2.
- `CHK-OBJ-3` — when `maturity` is not `placeholder`: the Mission holds no bracketed template text; at least one goal exists; every goal carries the four fields with in-enum `kind` and `status`; ids are contiguous from 1 and unique.
- `CHK-OBJ-4` — every Shifts row carries an ISO date and a `shifted` value that is `mission` or an existing `OBJ-N`; every `dropped` goal has a Shifts row naming it.
- `CHK-OBJ-5` (WARNING) — `reviewed_at` is older than `review_every_days`: the file is due for a human read.

An `OBJ-N` token in a review report, a brief, or an ADR is a reference to this file; `audit-docs` resolves it here and reports a dangling one as BROKEN.

**Populate gate.** Every skill that reads this file — `migrate-adrs`, the `cleanup-campsite` objectives nudge, the night gardener — checks it first. When the file is missing, or `maturity` is `placeholder`, the skill asks the owner to populate it: in a session with a human, ask once at the start with a pointer to this section, then continue with the work that does not depend on it; in an unattended session, write one line naming the gap in the output and skip the dependent step. Never invent a mission or a goal to unblock a step.

**Alignment before work and through delegation.** Every agent reads the resolved `<docs_dir>/objectives.md` before starting work, including small fixes, research, planning, and reviews. Commander and night gardener read it at startup and on resume, before selecting work or delegating. Resolve the tree through §14; never assume the literal `docs/` directory exists. A commander without shell access receives the resolved path from its caller.

Use the Mission and relevant active goals to assess the task's purpose, tradeoffs, and completion evidence. Respect the maturity ladder above; `exploring` goals remain hypotheses. Do not treat dropped goals as requirements. Explain how the task serves or preserves the mission or relevant goals in the existing task brief or result. A sentence suffices for a small task; no extra artifact or approval gate is required. Do not invent a goal association when none is supported.

Every delegation, including a forked skill invocation, carries the resolved objectives path and either the mission with relevant goal statements and measures, or an explicit instruction to read the file before work. Include known tensions and require recipients to preserve this context in further delegation. Do not assume session history or a role's installed prompt supplies it. Re-read the file when it changes during the work. Report a concrete conflict before dependent work proceeds; a conflict with an approved plan is a contradicted premise under §11. Objectives alone authorize no additional work and no edits to the objectives file.

Apply the populate gate above when objectives are unavailable. The gardener's turn gate runs before every other act, reads included, so a skipped turn reads nothing and stays silent; on a turn that proceeds it reads objectives before selecting work, and any missing-objectives notice waits for output the gate permits.

**Who writes what.** Humans own the Mission, Goals, and Shifts content. Claude seeds the placeholder at init, proposes edits in chat or via `docs/inbox/`, appends a Shifts row only on instruction, and bumps `reviewed_at` only after a human has read the file in that session.

### Operation log contract

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `6`.

Append-only, newest entries at the **top**. Each entry uses the exact prefix:

```
## [YYYY-MM-DD] <op> | <subject>
```

Op enum (exhaustive): `init | extract | arch | ingest | refresh | audit | cleanup-campsite | lint | adr | brief | journal | promptbook | invariant | observation | recover | query | schema | skill | origin | garden | adr-review | backfill | release`. (Long-lived trees may carry the legacy `cleanup` op spelling — what `cleanup-campsite` was formerly called — in historical log entries; `audit-docs` CHK-LOG-1 accepts both forms for backward compatibility on append-only history.)

#### Op-enum regex (canonical — single source of truth)

This block is the **single source of truth** for the `docs/log.md` op-enum regex. `audit-docs` (CHK-LOG-1, both the inline and Explore-agent paths) MUST reference this block by name rather than restating the pattern.

**A log op and a journal category are two enums.** `docs/log.md` records a skill *operation*, enumerated above. `docs/journal/YYYY-MM.md` records a work *category*, enumerated in §4. The two lists are independent, and one name can sit in both — `release` does. Adding a name to one enum leaves the other unchanged.

- **Current-writer regex** — what every skill MUST emit going forward. `cleanup-campsite` only; the legacy `cleanup` form is NOT permitted in new entries:

  ```
  ^## \[\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\] (init|extract|arch|ingest|refresh|audit|cleanup-campsite|lint|adr|brief|journal|promptbook|invariant|observation|recover|query|schema|skill|origin|garden|adr-review|backfill|release) \| 
  ```

- **Historical-reader regex** — what `audit-docs` accepts when validating append-only history. Identical to the current-writer regex except the legacy `cleanup` form is also tolerated (pre-rename entries are frozen history and must not be flagged):

  ```
  ^## \[\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\] (init|extract|arch|ingest|refresh|audit|cleanup-campsite|cleanup|lint|adr|brief|journal|promptbook|invariant|observation|recover|query|schema|skill|origin|garden|adr-review|backfill|release) \| 
  ```

**Changing either enum is not a one-line edit here.** The installed crux skills carry their own copy of both enums, and each does something different with it. `log-work` refuses a log op its copy does not carry, and writes nothing. It does NOT refuse an unknown journal category: it falls back to `misc` and warns, so the entry lands under the wrong name rather than not at all. `audit-docs` reports a heading outside either enum and edits neither — CHK-LOG-1 surfaces a log heading as drift, CHK-JR-1 a journal heading as a warning. `generate-journal-index.py` refuses a month file whose heading carries a category outside its tuple. An op or category added to this file alone therefore reaches none of them. Extending either enum is a change to the crux plugin rather than to this file.

- `init` — `init-docs` ran.
- `extract` — `extract-code-docs` regenerated `docs/code/`.
- `arch` — `derive-arch` regenerated the `arch` spine (`docs/arch/`). Body: N files re-emitted, the new spine hash, and the trigger. The derived-architecture concern (per §4); default-on for new repos, additive.
- `ingest` — a source landed in the research wiki.
- `refresh` — `refresh-research-sources` or `refresh-research-synthesis` ran.
- `audit` — full vault-walk by `audit-docs`.
- `cleanup-campsite` — `cleanup-campsite` regenerated `docs/whats_next.md`. Body: `N open (X P1, Y P2, Z P3), M closed, K dismissed` plus top-3 P1 ids.
- `lint` — drift-check / verification result. Distinct from `audit` — narrower and triggered by `verify-code-docs` or by `audit-docs` sub-checks.
- `adr` — ADR proposed, accepted, deprecated, or superseded.
- `brief` — either `propose-brief` scaffolded a brief under `docs/briefs/` (body: title + path + `status: draft`), or `transition-brief` transitioned a brief's status (body: `BRIEF-<slug>: <old-status> → <new-status>`).
- `journal` — `log-work` appended a journal entry.
- `promptbook` — a book-level OPERATION, not a step. The op keeps its enum entry and its meaning; only its cardinality changed. **Three write points in a book's life, and advancing a prompt is not one of them.** An authoring skill (`author-promptbook` / `dev-cycle` / `iterate` / `patch-cycle`) writes one op when the book is authored; `run-promptbook` writes one when a run STARTS; `archive-promptbook` writes one when the book archives. Authoring keeps its op because it IS an operation — the cardinality cut is aimed at the per-step entry, and a book authored but never run would otherwise leave no trace in the log at all. **Advancing a prompt writes none.** Postcondition: the per-prompt chronology stays reconstructable from the run snapshot's own `started`/`completed` timestamps, which are per-prompt and immutable — a reader walks the snapshot directory instead of grepping one file. (`run-promptbook` status also writes this op, but only on the deliberate `--markdown` artifact write.)
- `invariant` — `transition-invariant` dispositioned an invariant pin (ratify/reject/retire). Body: pin id, class, the transition. The machine-side `recover-invariants` candidate emit logs no op of its own; only the human ratification gate writes `invariant`. (Invariants concern, schema_version 4+.)
- `observation` — an observation record was created or transitioned. Body: record id, the operation, one line. Two human-invoked commands write it on creation — `propose-observation` (the reconstructed ramp) and `transition-decision ratify --as observation` (the mined ramp) — and `transition-observation` writes it on a disposition (ratify/reject/retire/decide). This op splits from `invariant` by artifact class, not by writer: an observation is a distinct record with its own id space (`OBS-NNNN`) and its own lifecycle (§17.2). (`recover` splits from `adr` for the opposite reason — the machine emit of a decision candidate is itself logged. No scan writes an observation file in any state, so no scan logs an `observation` op.) A fourth writer, the batch sign-off, writes one entry per signed batch under the subject grammar `survey batch <batch-id>`, with the sorted record ids in the body; the protocol is §17.5. That batch entry reuses this op and mints none, because `audit-docs` reads the target tree's own op enum. Observations concern, additive.
- `recover` — `recover-decisions` emitted N observed decision candidates into `<docs_dir>/arch/_recovered/state.yml`. Body: partition scanned, candidate count. NEVER ratifies — only `transition-decision` writes `adr` on the recovery path. Arch/decision-recovery.
- `query` — `query-docs` answered a question. Optional log entry; off by default.
- `schema` — `manifest.yml` schema changed (new concern enabled, language extractor added, etc.).
- `skill` — forge-skill authored, revised, or pruned a project-local skill under `.claude/skills/`. Body: gap one-liner, path, self-test outcome, forge-log pointer. The `skill` op is the act's sole op written directly by forge-skill; the accompanying `log-work` journal call writes its own standard `journal |` op recording the append, as for every journaled act — never a duplicate `skill` op. Added for the forge-skill capability-gap loop.
- `origin` — a skill (or group of skills) was ported into the project from an external source. Body: which skill(s), from what ref, on what date.
- `garden` — `tend-garden` wrote a morning note under `docs/garden/`. Body: note date, headline count, artifact count. Written immediately BEFORE the note (the op is the note's log_head anchor and corroboration).
- `adr-review` — historical decision-review operation. Existing entries preserve the review date, historical report path and recorded finding counts. The token remains valid in old logs and in the backlog category and finding-id prefix; `migrate-adrs` writes no new decision-review report or `adr-review` operation. Historical reports and their log entries remain unchanged.[^historical-reviews]
- `backfill` — a governs backfill batch sign-off ran, initial or correction. Body: the batch id and the affected ADR ids, carried as `ADRs: <sorted ids>` so the receipts↔log↔journal cross-validation joins all three surfaces by batch id and date. One entry per batch; written only by the backfill sign-off skill. Heading: `## [<signed-date>] backfill | <batch-id>` — the subject IS the batch id. Body carries `ADRs: <sorted ids>`. The paired journal hook is category `review`, subject `backfill sign-off <batch-id>`, in the signed month.
- `release` — a version was published to a release target. Body: the publication time carrying an explicit timezone, the version, the target repo, and the published revision. The heading date is the publication date in that same timezone, so the heading and the instant below it never name different days. A release published at 05:08 UTC therefore reads as the previous day in Mountain time, which is the day the person who ran it experienced. Name the zone rather than an offset, so a winter release reads MST and a summer one MDT. One entry per target, so a version that reaches the private beta and then the public repo carries two entries. The beta entry is written first, because a version that fails beta never reaches the public repo. A record written after the fact also names when it was recorded, so a reader can tell the act from the note of it. Written by whoever runs the release.

Body under the heading: 1–5 lines. List specific paths touched. Keep terse — `log.md` is for grep, not reading.

`grep "^## \[" docs/log.md` returns the chronology. `grep -oE "^## \[[^]]+\] \w+" docs/log.md | sort | uniq -c` returns per-op counts.

### Journal contract

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `journal (`.

- `docs/journal/YYYY-MM.md` — one file per month. Append-only. Greppable headings.
- Each entry: `## [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] <category> | <subject>` then 1–10 lines + optional `Refs: [[...]] [[...]]` line.
- Category enum: `decision | implementation | bug | learning | blocker | refactor | meeting | review | misc | release`.
- Skill: `log-work`. Triggers: "log work", "journal this", end-of-day, after a meaningful skill side-effect.
- **Body lines never begin with `## [`** — that prefix is reserved for entry headings. Any content that would start a body line with `## [` must be rewritten or dropped; otherwise it is indistinguishable from a real heading and can poison the retrospective window anchor.
- **A composed body never leaves a fence open** — judged by the shared fence subset in `crux/scripts/md_fences.py` over the composed body alone, not the body concatenated with existing file content. A fence line counts toward the 1–10 body budget, the same treatment the `Friction:` line already gets.
- **A body line may optionally begin `Friction:`, naming a specific friction in that unit of work** — one line, at most one per entry, sitting before the `Refs:` line when both are present, and counting as a body line toward the 1–10 budget; a line whose remainder is empty, including a bare `Friction: none`, is a contract violation, and the remedy is to omit the line entirely. See `rule:journal-friction-line`.
- Distinct from `docs/log.md`: the journal is *narrative work performed*; `log.md` is *skill operations*.

### Brief lifecycle and authorship

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `briefs (`.

- `docs/briefs/BRIEF-<slug>.md` is **pre-decision exploration**, authored **either** by a human (Claude scaffolds from `BRIEF-template.md`; the body is written by the user) **or** by the `whiteboarding` skill (the `brainstormer` agent produces a session that arrives via `docs/inbox/`, filed by `process-inbox` → `propose-brief`).
- ADRs cite briefs via `related_briefs:`. `audit-docs` enforces bidirectional consistency.
- Skills: `propose-brief` scaffolds the file + frontmatter + index rollup + `brief` log op, then stops (the body is human-authored); `transition-brief` closes the lifecycle (`draft → published | abandoned`), mutating only frontmatter (never the body), updating the rollup + writing a `brief` op. `init-docs` creates the directory; ADR workflows reference briefs.
- A brief with `status: draft` cited by an ADR triggers an `audit-docs` warning.

### Complete manifest contract

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `7`.

<!-- BEGIN EXAMPLE: manifest-contract -->
```yaml
schema_version: "5"

concerns_enabled:           # which concerns this project uses (seven default plus the default-on arch spine and observations)
  - code
  - research
  - adrs
  - briefs
  - journal
  - promptbooks
  - invariants              # enabled by default on new trees; opt-in on migration (§15)
  - arch                    # default-on for new repos; opt-in for existing trees (§4)
  - observations            # default-on for new repos; opt-in for existing trees (§17)

code:
  extractors:               # one entry per language; name → extractor plugin
    <language>:
      extractor: <plugin-name>     # matches scripts/extractors/<name>.py
      glob: "<glob>"               # string or list of strings
      include_private: true        # python only; any other key refuses the python run

research:
  refresh_interval_days: 90        # source-staleness threshold for refresh-research-sources

adr:
  next_number: 1                   # monotonic, never reused; allocated by propose-adr
  spec_rule_from: null             # OPTIONAL. The CHK-ADR-SPEC cohort boundary (§11.D):
                                   # null/absent = rule inert; NNNN = governs every ADR numbered >= NNNN.
  governs_from: null               # OPTIONAL. The governs-block cohort boundary: null/absent = no
                                   # governs block expected; NNNN = every ADR numbered >= NNNN is
                                   # expected to carry a governs block or a recorded exemption.
  governs_exempt: []               # OPTIONAL. List of ADR IDs excused from the governs-coverage
                                   # cohort even though their number is >= governs_from. Default [].
  governs_backfilled: {}           # OPTIONAL. The backfill admission ledger: {ADR-NNNN: [handles]},
                                   # append-only per handle — a removed handle is retained against
                                   # re-admission. Written ONLY by the backfill sign-off skill.
  governs_backfill_cohort: []      # OPTIONAL. The frozen backfill cohort: the enumerated ADR ids
                                   # (Accepted, non-archived, numbered below governs_from)
                                   # snapshotted when the backfill machinery lands; closed forever.
  governs_backfill_complete: ~     # OPTIONAL. Terminal binary marker: absent or `true`. Set only
                                   # when Σ backfilled + Σ no-rule = |cohort| over distinct ADRs;
                                   # any pending cohort ADR defeats it.
  governs_rule_baseline: []        # OPTIONAL. The rule-length advisory baseline (§11.D rule 7): the
                                   # ENUMERATED ADR ids that predate the advisory IN THIS TREE,
                                   # snapshotted once and closed from then on. `[]` is correct for a
                                   # new tree and self-maintaining — with no ADRs yet, every ADR you
                                   # write is advised on. ABSENT leaves the advisory inert, and the
                                   # governs-coverage gate says so in its `warnings`. Adopting it in
                                   # a tree that already has ADRs is a ONE-OFF snapshot of their ids,
                                   # not a list regenerated on each run and never grown to excuse a
                                   # newly written ADR.

arch:                              # OPTIONAL block. The arch concern's strict gate (§4).
  require:                         # OPTIONAL. The concerns this tree REQUIRES. Absent = no gate.
    - data-model                   # A concern named here whose RECORDED verdict is not `populated`
    - api-surface                  # fails the derive with exit 1 and its verdict on stdout, having
    - module-graph                 # written the spine. ALWAYS checked, no flag needed. `--strict` is
    - decision-index               # a separate route requiring EVERY concern for one run.
                                   # Name only concerns this repository already produces: requiring
                                   # one it does not would fail your own build. Read by
                                   # `derive-arch.py`, never by the deriver's `_build`, so it never
                                   # enters the arch source set and never flaps the drift gate.

journal:                           # OPTIONAL block. The friction-line cohort boundary.
  friction_line_from: null         # OPTIONAL. ISO date, nullable. null/absent = friction-line count
                                   # unmeasurable; a date sets the boundary at or after which a
                                   # `Friction:` count is measurable (rule:journal-friction-line).
                                   # init-docs writes the initialization date here, never null.

promptbook:
  next_number: 1                   # monotonic, never reused; allocated by every authoring skill, incl. a successor book

observation:                       # the observations concern (§17); present when `observations` is enabled
  next_number: 1                   # monotonic, never reused; allocated by propose-observation and by the
                                    # transition-decision observation terminal
  stale_days: 90                   # OPTIONAL. CHK-OBS-STALE's threshold, on the research.refresh_interval_days
                                    # model. Absent falls back to 90.
  next_survey_number: 1            # monotonic, never reused; allocated by the survey scaffold as the
                                    # SVY-NNNN batch id (§17.5). Machine-derived, never content-derived.
  survey_stub_days: 1              # OPTIONAL. The window in which a receipt recording no completion is
                                    # WARNING rather than BROKEN (§17.3, §17.5). Absent falls back to 1.

cleanup:                           # OPTIONAL block. Cleanup falls back to defaults if absent.
  adr_proposed_stale_days: 14      # Used by CLN-ADR-2 — flag Proposed ADRs older than this.
  stuck_promptbook_days: 14        # Used by CLN-PB-1 — flag promptbooks whose current_run snapshot mtime hasn't moved.
  audit_stale_days: 14             # Cleanup emits a P1 "run audit-docs" suggestion if audit hasn't run within this window.
  forged_skill_stale_days: 30      # no authored/revised/used/evaluated event within this window (timestamp comparison). Used by CLN-FG-1 and CLN-FG-2.
  retro_due_runs: 5                # Used by CLN-RETRO-1 — flag when ≥ this many books archived since the last 'Retrospective:' journal entry.
  adr_review_due_days: 7           # CLN-ADR-5 may suggest migrate-adrs when historical reviews are older than this; no pass is required. Absent falls back to 7.
```
<!-- END EXAMPLE: manifest-contract -->

`journal.friction_line_from` is prospective and per-tree, on the same cohort model `adr.spec_rule_from` already establishes. Absent or `null` leaves every friction reader `unmeasurable` — there is no boundary before which a zero count could mean anything. Set to an ISO date, it marks the boundary at or after which a `Friction:` line is expected wherever `log-work` is the writer; a reader counts only entries dated at or after it, and its `basis` says the window was truncated when the asked-about window starts earlier. The recorded date is not earlier than the date the conforming writer was in use in that tree — an earlier date reintroduces the ambiguity the boundary exists to remove. A tree `init-docs` creates records the initialization date here rather than `null`, so a fresh tree measures friction from its first conforming entry; a `--force` re-bootstrap carries the existing tree's recorded date forward rather than resetting it forward.

`schema_version` here governs the **`docs/` tree layout only** — it does NOT cover the plugin's SKILL.md frontmatter contract. That contract has its own `schema_version` under `plugin.json` (see §7.A). The two namespaces are intentionally separate: `docs/manifest.yml` schema bumps when this directory tree's layout changes; `plugin.json` schema bumps when SKILL.md frontmatter conventions change. A **third** version axis, the per-file **`format_version`** on promptbook/run documents (see §3), is distinct from both: it governs the intra-file structure of one promptbook/run YAML document (not a directory-tree layout and not the SKILL.md contract), so changing a promptbook/run file format bumps `format_version`, **never** this `schema_version`.

The installed plugin refuses to operate on a `docs/` tree whose `schema_version` is outside its supported range.

**`docs/manifest.yml` schema version history:**
- `"1"` — initial layout.
- `"2"` — Layout unchanged since v1 introduction; the bump aligned with a broader plugin-schema revision. Additive — v1 trees read cleanly under a v2 validator.
- `"3"` — **BREAKING — the first non-additive layout bump; it ends the additive-only precedent the `"1"`/`"2"` rows established** (do not read the rows above as asserting all bumps are additive). Retires the research-local `docs/research/new/` drop folder in favor of the cross-concern top-level `docs/inbox/` staging area processed by `process-inbox`. A v2 tree has `docs/research/new/` and no `docs/inbox/`; recognized now only as a needs-migration state. **Historical upgrade path on pinned public `v3.23.2`:** its `audit-docs --migrate` creates `docs/inbox/`, relocates any in-flight `docs/research/new/*` (incl. a pending `urls.md`) into it, removes the emptied `docs/research/new/`, and rewrites `schema_version` to `"3"`.
- `"4"` — BREAKING. Adds the seventh concern, **invariants** (§15): a ledger under `docs/invariants/` + a peer executable check suite at `<tree>/invariants/checks/` reconciled via the `.bionic.yml`-rooted manifest. Breaking because the peer suite lives *outside* the docs tree and an older plugin cannot gracefully degrade (ignoring an unreconciled suite risks treating durable checks as disposable). Superseded by `"5"`; recognized now only as a needs-migration state (rung 4→5). **Historical upgrade path on pinned public `v3.23.2`:** its `audit-docs --migrate` (rung 3→4) bumps to `"4"`, **opt-in-enables** `invariants` (only when the `bionic/` layout is present or you confirm — an existing repo with no `bionic/` degrades gracefully), and creates the empty ledger + suite + reconciliation surfaces (idempotent, fail-closed).
- `"5"` — **current. BREAKING.** Unifies the whole tree under `bionic/` and retires `docs/` as a layout name. Concerns sit directly under `bionic/`. The invariants concern becomes one folder — `<docs_dir>/invariants/`, with `checks/` and `reconciliation.yml` inside. The default `docs_dir` becomes `bionic`, and `init-docs` writes an explicit `.bionic.yml` for every tree it creates. A tree at a custom `docs_dir` is still a valid `"5"` tree. The upgraded plugin operates only on `"5"` (the supported-range predicate is the single-value check `schema_version == "5"`) and recognizes `"4"`/`"3"`/`"2"` solely as needs-migration states. **Historical upgrade path on pinned public `v3.23.2`:** its `audit-docs --migrate` (rung 4→5, implemented there by `crux/scripts/migrate-tree.py`) folds the check suite into `invariants/checks/`, merges the tree entry-by-entry into `bionic/` with `manifest.yml` moved last, merges (never overwrites) the config, and sets `schema_version: "5"` (idempotent, fail-closed, resumable). Existing `docs/` trees keep resolving via bare-directory discovery with zero config and no migration.

The plugin's SKILL.md frontmatter contract (see §7.A) was revised separately, bumping `plugin.json` `schema_version` from `"1"` to `"2"` — `docs/manifest.yml` `schema_version` did not move because no `docs/` layout changed. Likewise the `cleanup-campsite` additions (the log op, the regenerated `docs/whats_next.md`, the optional `cleanup:` block above) were **additive** — older readers gracefully degrade (the new op shows as a `CHK-LOG-*` warning at worst; absent `whats_next.md` is the v1 default; absent `cleanup:` block falls back to defaults) — and did not bump this `schema_version`. The promptbook/run Markdown→YAML format change is a `format_version` change, NOT a tree-layout bump: the files still live at `promptbooks/active/`, `promptbooks/runs/<id>-<slug>/`, `promptbooks/archive/` — only their extension and intra-file shape changed, and legacy `.md` files coexist with new `.yaml` ones.

### ADR frontmatter and governs

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `11.A`.

This table is the **single source of truth** for ADR frontmatter. The plugin's `templates/ADR-template.md`, `propose-adr`, and `audit-docs` (CHK-ADR-1) MUST reference this table by name rather than restating the field list. `audit-docs` CHK-ADR-1a compares the template's frontmatter keyset against this table and WARNs on divergence.

The field-name column uses backtick markup so the comparison is mechanical (extract the backticked tokens from the first table column = the canonical keyset).

| field | type | required? | semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | `ADR-NNNN`, 4-digit zero-padded, optionally carrying the repo's configured artifact prefix per §14.3 (e.g. `CRX-ADR-NNNN`). Matches filename. |
| `title` | string | required | Declarative present-tense decision title. |
| `status` | enum | required | `Proposed \| Accepted \| Deprecated \| Superseded`. |
| `date` | ISO date | required | Date of the current status entry. Moves on every transition. |
| `proposed_date` | ISO date | required | Immutable; date first Proposed. |
| `acceptance_format` | string | required for new-policy ADRs; absent historically | `crux.adr-acceptance.v1` requires validated acceptance evidence before its rules govern. Missing evidence never falls back to historical acceptance. |
| `accepted_date` | ISO date \| null | required | Set on accept; `null` until then. |
| `deprecated_date` | ISO date \| null | required | Set on deprecate; `null` until then. |
| `superseded_date` | ISO date \| null | required | Set on supersede; `null` until then. |
| `supersedes` | list | required | ADR ids this ADR replaces (insertion-ordered; `[]` if none). |
| `superseded_by` | string \| null | required | The single ADR id that replaced this one, or `null`. |
| `deciders` | list | required | ≥1 handle. |
| `tags` | list | required | Topic tags. |
| `related_briefs` | list | required | `BRIEF-<slug>` filenames; `[]` if none. |
| `related_research` | list | required | research page references; `[]` if none. Each entry is a path relative to `docs/research/`: a bare `<slug>` means `sources/<slug>.md`; a `<category>/<slug>` means a `docs/research/<category>/<slug>.md` synthesis page. Resolved (with a fail-closed containment grammar) by `audit-docs` CHK-ADR-9. |
| `amends` | list | optional | ADR ids this ADR narrowly refines (one-way; predecessors not mutated). Omit or `[]` if none. |
| `governs` | list | optional | Structured rule records this ADR authors; each entry is a mapping (sub-fields below). A MAY, authored at Proposed time. Cohort-bounded by the tree's governs cohort boundary. |

Each `governs` entry is a mapping with seven sub-fields — `domain`, `rule`, `scope`, `handle`, `anchor`, `provenance`, `retires` — never top-level frontmatter keys in their own right:

```yaml
governs:
  - domain: decision-doctrine
    rule: "each ADR's governing rule is authored once in a governs block and projected deterministically"
    scope: the ADR frontmatter schema + the summaries projection
    handle: ADR-NNNN/governs-block
    anchor: "each ADR's governing rule is authored once"
    provenance: authored
```

The `handle` value above is illustrative shape only — a live handle is `ADR-NNNN/<rule-slug>`, anchored to the ADR that authors it. The `anchor` value is equally illustrative: a live anchor must quote the ADR's own body.

`anchor` is a verbatim span — a string, or a list of strings — quoted from the ADR body and verified by **space-folded containment**: collapse each whitespace run to a single space and strip the ends, on both the anchor and the body, before comparison; a list anchor requires every element to contain independently (AND, never OR), and a repeated span contains by membership. `anchor` is **required** on entries whose ADR number is below the tree's governs cohort boundary (the backfill cohort — the extraction binds a span of a body frozen before the contract existed) and **expected absent** on prospective entries, whose mutable body offers no verification target. An empty anchor is a validation error in every shape: an empty or whitespace-only string, an empty list, or an empty or whitespace-only list element.

`retires` is an OPTIONAL list of rule handles this entry displaces. A retired handle leaves the rule table's live rows, leaves the resolver, and leaves the doctrine index, and appears instead in the rule table's `## Retired handles` roster with its rule text intact — the record survives the retirement. Retirement is one-way and clause-scoped: it never mutates the retired entry's own ADR, whose frontmatter and body stay untouched. It is a state rather than an event, so two ADRs retiring one handle, and one ADR naming a handle twice, are both idempotent. Five refusals are fail-closed, because a silent one would make the retirement unauditable. An entry may not retire a handle from its own ADR's `governs` block. It may not retire a handle that any signed record in `docs/adrs/doctrine/reconciliations.yml` names, so a retirement cannot orphan a human signature. A `retires` target that has never been a live handle fails the projection as a typo. That resolution checks the live handles, the retired roster, the archived ADR tier, and the removed roster. The archived tier is in that history so a settled retirement survives its target's ADR being archived. A handle appearing in both the removed lane and the retired lane fails. A sub-field outside the seven named above fails, so a mistyped `retires` is refused rather than dropped. The lane boundary: `removed` is a human withdrawing an admission through the receipts manifest and presupposes the handle has left its ADR's frontmatter, while `retired` is a later decision displacing a rule that stays on the record. `retires` sits deliberately OUTSIDE the six-field `content_digest` — a retirement is a relation between handles, not the content of the rule beside it — so every signed receipt and every signed reconciliation stays valid across one.

`provenance` reuses the invariants concern's enum unchanged (§15.2: `authored | recovered | reconstructed`) — this table mints no second enum. The decided-vs-observed authority a `governs` entry carries is derived from `provenance` (`authored` → decided; `recovered` or `reconstructed` → observed), never a separate stored field.

Adding a frontmatter field is a one-row edit here plus a matching edit to the plugin's `templates/ADR-template.md`; CHK-ADR-1a catches the two falling out of sync.

### ADR body contract

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `11.D`.

**This section is the single statement of the rule.** `${CRUX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/ADR-template.md`, `propose-adr`, and `audit-docs` (`CHK-ADR-SPEC`) carry a pointer to it and never a copy — §11.A's name-it-once discipline applied to the rule about naming things once. §11.A governs an ADR's frontmatter; this section governs what its body may contain. The writing rules the `prose-review` skill carries govern how a sentence in it is written.

The seven numbered rules below are **§11.D's own numbering**. Cite this section by rule number; if your tree records the deciding ADR separately, do not read its clause numbers as these rule numbers.

**1. A body states requirements and postconditions, never implementation recipe.** An ADR says what must be true when the work is done. It may bind a mechanism when the mechanism **is** the decision — a protocol, a storage engine, a wire format, a published interface — because that choice is disputable on architectural grounds. It may not say how a chosen thing is driven: call signatures, serializer options, exact file contents, command recipes, code. Those are disputable only on syntax, and they belong to the dev module, where a type checker and a test suite review them. Where one of them **is** the contract being decided, the carve-out governs and the prohibition does not.

**2. Executed measurements are informative, not normative.** A body may record evidence it measured rather than reasoned — settings tried, values produced — in a footnote marked **informative**. Such a footnote binds no implementation: any implementation meeting the stated requirements conforms.

**3. The four narrative sections carry a 120-line budget.** The budget spans `## Context` through the last line before `## References` — Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered and Consequences together. `## References` and any footnote block sit outside it.

It is a **tripwire for rule 1, not a quality bar.** An over-budget body is a signal to re-read for embedded recipe; it is never a defect on its own, and there is no cap. A body that is over budget on purpose declares why, in one blockquote line immediately under its `## Context` heading:

```markdown
## Context

> **Body budget:** 164 lines — three coordinate migrations whose ordering constraint is the decision.
```

A body over budget **with** that line is not a finding. A body over budget **without** one is a `CHK-ADR-SPEC` WARNING. An ADR that is itself a source of truth for a shape (rule 4) is exempt from the budget.

**4. Name the source of truth; do not restate it.** A body may name a schema file, a contract section, or an index as the source of truth for a shape, and must not restate that shape inline — the same discipline §11.A applies to ADR frontmatter and §11.B to the run-snapshot shape. **Postcondition:** the pointer stays resolvable to the intended artifact after the body freezes. Inside this tree that means naming an artifact that carries a drift gate; outside it, naming a stable identifier such as a versioned standard rather than a location.

**5. A path inside a frozen ADR body is history, not drift.** A body past `Proposed` is frozen, so a path it cites records what was true when the decision was made. Cleanup does not report that class; a rule that did was retired outright, and any standing dismissals stay in `docs/whats_next.md` as history. Rule 4's postcondition keeps new bodies safe going forward and is not retroactive.

**6. Route a convention a check can carry to the invariants concern.** A decision whose whole content is a convention an executable check can carry belongs in the invariants concern (§15) rather than in an ADR. Guidance for the drafting architect; it adds no gate.

**7. Write the shortest ADR that fully states the decision, its scope, and its consequences.** Use simple, precise prose. Keep each `governs` rule to one obligation and its necessary conditions; put rationale and examples in the body. Brevity must not change the meaning.

### The prospective cohort

`CHK-ADR-SPEC` is **prospective only**. Every body written before the rule existed is exempt, permanently — a frozen body cannot be brought into compliance, and reporting one would be noise that never clears.

The boundary is a per-tree number, `adr.spec_rule_from` in `docs/manifest.yml` (§7). Absent or `null` means this tree never adopted the rule and `CHK-ADR-SPEC` reports nothing at all. Set to `NNNN` means the rule governs every ADR numbered **≥ `NNNN`**. ADR numbers are monotonic and never reused, so a number is a clean cohort boundary in a way a date is not.

The boundary is configurable while the 120-line budget is not, for two reasons. The cohort is inherently per-tree: an ADR number means nothing across trees, and a tree adopting the rule today needs its own boundary. The budget is a convention crux ships, so it has one value — and `audit-docs/SKILL.md` is a distributed surface that may carry no ADR identifier at all, which is a second reason the boundary cannot be a literal in the rule's own text.

**Adopting the rule in an existing tree:** set `adr.spec_rule_from` to the next number `propose-adr` will allocate, so the cohort starts empty and the rule reports nothing until the first body written under it. Measure the in-cohort bodies before fixing the value if you set it lower.

### Invariant frontmatter

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `15.2`.

Required keyset on every `<docs_dir>/invariants/<slug>.md` (the canonical contract `audit-docs` enforces):

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | `INV-NNNN` (4-digit, zero-padded; optional artifact prefix per §14.3). Matches the pin; unique. |
| `class` | enum | `data \| shape \| behavior \| contract \| experience` (the five invariant classes). |
| `provenance` | enum | `authored \| recovered \| reconstructed` (origin). |
| `ratification` | enum | `observed \| ratified \| rejected \| retired`. Machine-recovered pins enter `observed`; only a human transitions (§15.3). |
| `verification` | mapping | v1 field `last_result` ∈ `pass \| fail \| stale \| none` (the aggregate per §15.4). Strength grades are a deferred follow-on. |
| `related_adrs` | list | the *why*-link; ADR ids or `[]`. |
| `related_briefs` | list | brief slugs or `[]`. |
| `checks` | list | `check_id`s in the suite (possibly empty). |

The four ladder names (`observed-unratified`, `recovered-and-ratified`, …) are **derived rendering views** over (provenance, ratification, verification), never stored enums.

### Invariant reconciliation

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `15.4`.

The reconciliation manifest, `reconciliation.yml`, lives at `<docs_dir>/invariants/reconciliation.yml` — beside the ledger, NOT inside `checks/` — and is the single reconciliation surface `audit-docs` reads. One **entry per check**, v1 shape:

```yaml
{ check_id: <stable path/id in <docs_dir>/invariants/checks/>, pin_id: INV-NNNN, last_result: pass|fail|stale|none, last_checked: <ISO date|null> }
```

The check→pin mapping is derived (regenerable); `last_result`/`last_checked` are authored data persisted here (crux is **not** a test runner — a human/CI annotation or a check's recorded exit sets them). A **resolvable check** = a `check_id` present in `<docs_dir>/invariants/checks/` whose entry maps to an existing pin.

**Pin-level aggregation** (a pin with 0..N checks): `fail` if any check is `fail`; else `stale` if any is `stale`; else `pass` if ≥1 is `pass` and none fail/stale; else `none`.

### Observation frontmatter

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `17.1`.

This table is the **single source of truth** for observation frontmatter, on the §11.A model. Adding a field is a one-row edit here. The field-name column uses backtick markup so the comparison is mechanical: the backticked tokens in the first column are the canonical keyset.

| field | type | required? | semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required | `OBS-NNNN`, 4-digit zero-padded, optionally carrying the repo's configured artifact prefix per §14.3. Matches the filename. Allocated from `observation.next_number` (§7); never reused. |
| `title` | string | required | Declarative present-tense statement of what the code does. |
| `status` | enum | required | `observed \| ratified \| rejected \| retired \| decided`. |
| `date` | ISO date | required | Date of the current status entry. Moves on every transition. |
| `observed_date` | ISO date | required | Immutable; date the record was first written. |
| `ratified_date` | ISO date \| null | required | Set on ratify; `null` until then. |
| `rejected_date` | ISO date \| null | required | Set on reject; `null` until then. |
| `retired_date` | ISO date \| null | required | Set on retire; `null` until then. |
| `decided_date` | ISO date \| null | required | Set on the `decided` transition; `null` until then. |
| `provenance` | enum | required | `recovered \| reconstructed`. The §15.2 enum minus `authored`: an authored rule is an ADR, so `authored` on an observation is a validation error. |
| `decided_by` | string \| null | required | The ADR id that records this rule as a decision, or `null`. Non-null exactly when `status` is `decided`. |
| `evidence` | list | required | One or more `path:line-range` strings, each repo-relative — for example `crux/scripts/summaries_projection.py:1240-1268`. Never a code excerpt, and never prose quoting one. |
| `anchor_id` | string | required | The structural anchor identity, `sha256(anchor_kind + NUL + canonical_anchor)[:16]`, on **every** record including a reconstructed one. It is what makes a re-mine recognize a fact already recorded. |
| `related_invariants` | list | required | `INV-NNNN` ids, or `[]`. |
| `tags` | list | required | Topic tags. |
| `governs` | list | required | One or more rule records, each a mapping using the §11.A `governs` sub-fields unchanged. Four constraints apply here and nowhere else: each entry's `provenance` equals the record's `provenance`; each entry's `handle` is namespaced by the record id, `OBS-NNNN/<rule-slug>`, so a handle cannot collide across records or with an ADR handle; `anchor` is unused, because a record's claim is bound to code by `anchor_id` rather than to a body span — an `anchor` sub-field on an observation entry is a validation error; and `retires` is unused on an observation entry, because an observation describes what the code does and cannot displace a decided rule — a `retires` sub-field on an observation entry is a validation error. |

The body below the frontmatter is prose for a human: what the code does, where the evidence is, and why this is observed rather than decided. It carries no code excerpt either.

### Observation lifecycle

Source extract: `crux/templates/AGENTS.md.tmpl`, section `17.2`.

The state machine is the invariants ratification machine (§15.3) plus one terminal:

```
observed ──ratify──▶ ratified ──retire──▶ retired
   │                     │
   │                     └──decide──▶ decided
   └──reject──▶ rejected
```

| From | Op | To | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| observed | ratify | ratified | A human affirms the record describes the code. |
| observed | reject | rejected | A human judges the record wrong or not worth keeping. |
| ratified | retire | retired | The code moved away from what the record describes. |
| ratified | decide | decided | A human authored an ADR for the same rule; `decided_by` names it. |

Every other transition is refused. The lifecycle is forward-only, there is no path back into `observed`, and a revived observation is a new record.

**The writer boundary is human-invoked against scan, not one component.** An observation file is created and mutated only by a human-invoked command. **No scan writes an observation file in any state.** Two commands create one — `transition-decision ratify --as observation` on the mined ramp and `propose-observation` on the reconstructed ramp — and both are human-invoked. Two commands mutate one. `transition-observation` remains the **only single-record route** past `observed`, and the batch sign-off is the **only batch route**, equivalent to N individual ratifications under one signed receipt (§17.5). `transition-observation` keeps its batch refusal verbatim and redirects to the sign-off, because a refusal made conditional on a flag is a false green over the safety property. The extraction path creates neither an observation nor an ADR; it writes only its own candidate state file.

**A ratified record's claim is immutable.** Its `governs` rule, `domain`, `scope`, `provenance`, `evidence`, and `anchor_id` never change. Only the lifecycle fields change, and only through the gate. A re-mine that finds a recorded `anchor_id` carrying different rule text or different evidence therefore revises nothing: it opens a **successor candidate** in the candidate state file, on that same `anchor_id`, and a human ratifies the successor and retires its predecessor, or rejects it.

**Anchor loss is a signal, never a transition.** A re-mine that no longer finds a recorded `anchor_id` writes a stale-anchor signal to its own candidate state file. It does not touch the observation. A human retires the record through the gate.

### Research source registry

Source extract: `crux/skills/ingest-research/SKILL.md`, section 6c.

Add **one new row at the top of the table** (immediately after the separator line) with these exact column values, in order:

| Column | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `slug` | the source's slug |
| `title` | the frontmatter `title:` |
| `source_url` | the frontmatter `source_url:`, or `—` if null |
| `captured_at` | today (`YYYY-MM-DD`) |
| `last_source_check` | today (same as captured_at on first ingest) |
| `last_update` | `—` (always on first ingest; populated by `refresh-research-sources`) |
| `static` | `true` / `false` / `n/a` (last one when `source_url` is `—`) |
| `raw_path` | `research/raw/<today>/<slug>/` (relative to `docs/`) |
| `wiki_path` | `research/sources/<slug>.md` (relative to `docs/`) |

Newest-first ordering. Do not sort or rewrite older rows — only prepend.

## Appendix B. Embedded JSON Schemas

Each block includes the complete canonical schema and its local definitions.
Its `$ref` values resolve offline within that block. `$schema` identifies the
dialect; it is not a requirement to fetch a document. Source paths and hashes
identify the version reproduced here, not runtime dependencies.

The schemas cover current cycles (1/2), queue (1), test evidence (1/2), current
council formats declared in their discriminators, and historical ADR provenance
(1). Read discriminator values from each complete schema. A structurally valid
object does not establish an executed test, genuine approval, or valid transition.
Cross-field and lifecycle requirements in the guide apply in addition to schemas.

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",

                  ],

                  }
                }
              }
            },
            "packages": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "lock": {
                  "type": "object",

                  "properties": {

                      "const": "uv.lock"
                    },
                    "source": {
                      "enum": [
                        "subject",

                      ]
                    },
                    "project": {
                      "type": "boolean"
                    },
                    "dev": {
                      "type": "boolean"
                    },
                    "groups": {
                      "type": "array",
                      "items": {
                        "type": "string"
                      }
                    },
                    "extras": {
                      "type": "array",
                      "items": {
                        "type": "string"
                      }
                    }
                  }
                },
                "pins": {
                  "type": "array",
                  "items": {
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*==[^\\s;]+$"
                  }
                }
              },
              "additionalProperties": false
            },
            "isolated": {
              "type": "boolean"

            "tools": {
              "type": "array",

                "type": "string",

              }
            },

            },

              "type": "object",

            },
            "freshness_seconds": {
              "type": "number",
              "minimum": 0
            }
          }
        }
      }

    "fingerprint": {

          "type": "object"
        },

          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "additionalProperties": false
    },

      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
    },
    "revision": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },

      "type": "array",

        "type": "string"
      }
    },

      "type": "number"
    },

      "type": "number"
    },

      "type": "number",
      "minimum": 0
    },
    "status": {
      "enum": [
        "passed",
        "failed",
        "inputs-changed",
        "interrupted"
      ],

    },
    "returncode": {
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ],
      "description": "null when the child never started (a launch error)."
    },
    "reason": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    },
    "output": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^TE-[0-9a-f]{32}\\.log$"
    },
    "output_sha256": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
    },
    "record_sha256": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
    },
    "signal": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "The signal the engine received (SIGINT or SIGTERM) when it recorded an interrupted run."
    },
    "source_revision": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "lock_sha256": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ],
      "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
    },
    "tools": {
      "type": "object",
      "description": "Each registered tool's resolved path and --version first line, keyed by executable name."
    },
    "environment": {
      "type": [
        "object",
        "null"
      ],
      "description": "The identity file the capture wrapper wrote before the entry ran: implementation, version, marker_environment, sys_prefix, sys_flags, warnoptions, xoptions, filesystem_encoding, preferred_encoding, distributions and per-variable digests of normalized values. null for a non-Python check or a run that wrote none."
    }
  },
  "description": "Receipt of one execution of a registered or focused check. schema_version 2 records the executing process's environment (environment), the resolved tool versions (tools), the sha256 of the lock the requirement names (lock_sha256) and the dev checkout's HEAD (source_revision); the reader requires those four fields at version 2. A version 1 receipt is history: it is readable and complete-able, but lookup never counts it as a pass or a block."
}

### crux ADR provenance record (schema 1)

Source: `crux/schemas/adr-provenance.schema.json`  
Source SHA-256: `c1d994bfad185bd675d89ec4d9f664906e2c6ab8cbb8b0ccb027f870db7b474c`

<!-- BEGIN EXAMPLE: adr-provenance.schema.json -->
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "crux ADR provenance record (schema 1)",
  "description": "One record per ADR accepted inside a run, at <docs_dir>/adrs/provenance/ADR-NNNN.yaml. It names the run whose ADR module accepted the ADR and that run's base_commit, and gives each governs rule its standing. Each rule carries entry, its governs entry as accepted, and base, its governs entry at base_commit; both omit handle. A rule absent from the ADR at base_commit is guidance and has a null base. A rule present there is binding at its base entry, and an in-run edit to any of its fields but provenance is guidance. A rule present at base_commit that the run deleted is listed in removed_in_run and stays binding at its base entry until the owner promotes the deletion. An ADR first proposed inside the run has no base_path, so every rule is guidance. Promotions are appended from the owner's own instruction, quoted verbatim with its date. A promotion never changes base: a promoted rule is binding at its entry, and a promoted deletion takes effect. The summaries and doctrine projections read standing from these records and never from git history. The parser in crux/scripts/adr_provenance.py enforces this shape and the cross-field rules a JSON Schema cannot state.",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": [
    "schema",
    "adr",
    "run",
    "base_commit",
    "base_path",
    "base_sha256",
    "rules",
    "removed_in_run",
    "promotions"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "schema": {
      "const": "1"
    },
    "adr": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^ADR-[0-9]{4}$"
    },
    "run": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": [
        "book_id",
        "run_id",
        "snapshot"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "book_id": {
          "type": "string",
          "pattern": "^(?:[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}-)?PB-[0-9]{4}$"
        },
        "run_id": {
          "type": "string",
          "pattern": "^RUN-[0-9]{3,}$"
        },
        "snapshot": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        }
      }
    },
    "base_commit": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})$"
    },
    "base_path": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "base_sha256": {
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ],
      "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$"
    },
    "rules": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "required": [
          "handle",
          "standing",
          "entry",
          "base"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "handle": {
            "type": "string",
            "pattern": "^ADR-[0-9]{4}/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
          },
          "standing": {
            "enum": [
              "binding",
              "guidance"
            ]
          },
          "entry": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/entry",
            "description": "The rule's governs entry as accepted, without its handle."
          },
          "base": {
            "oneOf": [
              {
                "type": "null"
              },
              {
                "$ref": "#/$defs/entry"
              }
            ],
            "description": "The rule's governs entry at base_commit, without its handle; null for a guidance rule. A promotion leaves it unchanged."
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "removed_in_run": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "required": [
          "handle",
          "base"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "handle": {
            "type": "string",
            "pattern": "^ADR-[0-9]{4}/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
          },
          "base": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/entry",
            "description": "The deleted rule's governs entry at base_commit, at which it binds until the owner promotes the deletion."
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "promotions": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "required": [
          "date",
          "instruction",
          "handles",
          "body"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "date": {
            "type": "string",
            "pattern": "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$",
            "description": "The date of the owner's instruction."
          },
          "instruction": {
            "type": "string",
            "minLength": 1,
            "description": "The owner's own words, verbatim. An agent report, a run note or a council verdict is never this instruction."
          },
          "handles": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "string",
              "pattern": "^ADR-[0-9]{4}/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
            },
            "description": "The rules, and the deletions, whose in-run change this promotion makes binding."
          },
          "body": {
            "type": "boolean",
            "description": "True records that the owner promoted the ADR's in-run body passages. No projection reads it, because the projections read governs rules only."
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "$defs": {
    "entry": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": [
        "rule"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "domain": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "rule": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1
        },
        "scope": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "anchor": {
          "oneOf": [
            {
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        "provenance": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "retires": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
<!-- END EXAMPLE: adr-provenance.schema.json -->
